- Redistribution decision: Allowed under GPL-3.0-or-later, as for corpus C (`benchmarks/corpus/xyce`): the decks are redistributed verbatim as separate benchmark data files with the upstream copyright/licence notice and the complete GPLv3 text alongside them. They are test inputs, not linked into or distributed with any MIT-licensed spice-ts package. Decks that carry their own copyright or licence notice are excluded and not committed.

## Selection

- Candidates: 4133; selected: 128; excluded: 4005.
- Exclusions by reason: already-in-corpus 22, duplicate-content 352, licence 24, not-utf8 0, host-command 0, not-self-contained 544, no-analysis 155, ngspice-no-reference 2073, directory-cap 835.
- ngspice probe: ngspice-47, 60 s bound; receipt `benchmarks/corpus/corpus-g/ngspice-probe.json` (SHA-256 `b28cac6b90421d8f8a37cc241e76ebe5df7895b94b609662ae0629af7ed5ffa6`).

- Candidates: every git-tracked file under Netlists/ at the pinned revision whose name ends in .cir, .sp, .net, .ckt or .spi.
- already-in-corpus: the upstream path is already a source of another corpus manifest (corpus C `xyce`, `xyce-spice3`), or the bytes (or the bytes without a terminal newline) hash-match any fixture of an existing public corpus (classic, ngspice, xyce, corpus-d/e/f and the SPICE3 translations).
- duplicate-content: the bytes hash-match an earlier candidate (paths sorted); the first path is kept.
- licence: the deck carries a copyright or licence notice (vendor model text and similar) that the suite-wide GPL-3.0-or-later grant cannot be assumed to cover. Not committed.
- not-utf8: the bytes are not lossless UTF-8, so spice-ts cannot receive the identical deck through its string API.
- host-command: the deck runs shell or gnuplot commands on the host.
- not-self-contained: the deck loads another file (.include/.lib/OSDI) or names a sibling upstream file, so it cannot run unchanged in an isolated directory.
- no-analysis: no analysis card or control-block analysis command.
- ngspice-no-reference: ngspice-47 run on the identical bytes (batch mode, 60 s bound) did not exit 0 with at least one op/dc/ac/tran/pz/noise/disto plot in its raw file, so there is no reference to compare against. The probe result and ngspice's first error line are recorded in ngspice-probe.json. spice-ts is not run during selection.
- directory-cap: at most 1 deck(s) per suite directory (Netlists/<suite>, subdirectories included), first in path order, among decks that passed every rule above. Capped decks are listed below for later batches.

## Skipped sources

- KiCad eeschema simulation demos (`demos/simulation` of KiCad 10.0.5, https://gitlab.com/kicad/code/kicad/-/tree/master/demos/simulation): The demos ship `.kicad_sch` schematics, not SPICE decks: a netlist would be a kicad-cli-generated derivative (an adaptation, and its bytes depend on the KiCad version). Most demos also load vendor model libraries (AD8051, AD8009, LM317, OPA1641, IRF VDMOS, GaN Systems and ST SiC PSpice models) whose own notices the KiCad licence cannot be assumed to cover. Skipped; a later batch can commit generated netlists for the demos that use only built-in models, with the generator command recorded.
- ISCAS-85/89 combinational and sequential benchmark netlists: Gate-level `.bench` files, not SPICE: running them needs a transistor-level translation with a chosen cell library, which is an adaptation this batch avoids. The MCNC/CircuitSim90 transistor-level decks that the Xyce suite redistributes are in scope instead (one per suite directory here, the rest listed as directory-cap).
- Openly licensed textbook circuits (for example Lessons In Electric Circuits, Design Science License): The netlists are embedded in prose, so extracting them is an adaptation, and each would need a per-book licence review. Not evaluated in this batch.
- Vendor application notes and LTspice example circuits: Their terms do not grant redistribution. Skipped (link-only at most).
- Xyce Regression decks with their own copyright or licence notice: Listed below as `licence` exclusions and not committed.
